problems.title: Existence of a sine equation solution
problems.question: For which a does 7sin x=a−3 have a real solution?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The sine range is [−1,1].
steps: −7≤a−3≤7 gives −4≤a≤10. Every value in this interval is attained.

problems.title: Period of a shifted sine
problems.question: Find the least positive period of 5sin(3x+7)+11.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: For nonzero A,B, A sin(Bx+C)+D has period 2π/|B|.
steps: B=3, so the least positive period is 2π/3; the amplitude and shifts do not change it.

problems.title: Third term of a ninth-power expansion
problems.question: Find the third term of (2x+3)⁹.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The term is C(9,2)(2x)⁷3².
steps: C(9,2)=36=2²3². Multiplying with 2⁷3² gives 2⁹3⁴x⁷.

problems.title: Complementary line-plane and line-normal angles
problems.question: Find the sum of a line’s smaller angle to a plane and its smaller angle to a normal line of that plane.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Parallel and perpendicular components form a right triangle.
steps: If the inclination is theta, the normal-direction angle is 90°−theta. Their sum is 90°, also in the limiting parallel or normal cases.

problems.title: Projected area of a regular hexagon
problems.question: A regular hexagon of side 1 lies in a plane at 30° to another plane. Find its orthogonal projection area.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Projection area=original area×cos(angle between planes).
steps: The original area is 3√3/2. Multiply by cos30°=√3/2 to obtain 9/4.

problems.title: Length of twice one vector plus another
problems.question: |a|=2,|b|=1 and their angle is 60°. Find |2a+b|.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: a·b=2×1×cos60°=1. The squared length is 16+1+4=21.

problems.title: Power reduction of a sine square
problems.question: Simplify sin²3alpha+1.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: sin²t=(1−cos2t)/2.
steps: Adding 1 to the power-reduction formula gives (3−cos6alpha)/2.

problems.title: Maximum with two independent angles
problems.question: Maximize 3sin alpha+4sin(π/2+alpha)+sin beta.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: sin(π/2+alpha)=cos alpha; maximum of 3sin alpha+4cos alpha is 5.
steps: The first part reaches 5 when sin alpha=3/5,cos alpha=4/5. Independently choose sin beta=1.
The total maximum 5+1=6 is attained.

problems.title: A point’s planar projection distance to a line
problems.question: A is distance 7 from a plane and 9 from a line in it. B is the perpendicular foot on the plane. Find B’s line distance.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: By the three-perpendicular relationship, 9²=7²+d².

problems.title: Maximum reflection axes of a triangle
problems.question: What is the maximum number of symmetry axes a triangle can have?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: A triangle reflection axis must pass through a vertex and the midpoint of its opposite side.
steps: There are only three vertices, giving at most three axes. An equilateral triangle has all three, so the bound is attained.

problems.title: An exact floor value outside the cosine range
problems.question: Solve floor(cot(π/8)−tan(π/8))=cos x.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: cot t−tan t=2cot2t.
steps: The expression is 2cot(π/4)=2 exactly, so its floor is 2. Cosine cannot equal 2.

problems.title: Four distinct occupied train carriages
problems.question: Four passengers occupy distinct randomly selected carriages among nine. Find the probability the occupied set is {3,5,7,9}.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Every four-carriage subset is equally likely; there are C(9,4)=126.
steps: Only one occupied set is specified. Probability=1/126. Equivalently, 4! favourable passenger assignments divided by 9×8×7×6 total assignments gives the same result.

problems.title: A strict inequality required at every x
problems.question: Which listed alpha interval ensures √(x²−4x+4)>2cos alpha−1 for every real x?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The left side is |x−2|, with minimum zero.
steps: The inequality holds for every x iff 0>2cos alpha−1, or cos alpha<1/2.
The full set is (π/3+2kπ,5π/3+2kπ). The listed interval (π/3,5π/3) is one such complete cycle.

problems.title: A vector parallel to a cross product
problems.question: a=(2,1,4),b=(3,−2,1),c=(3,m,n). If c is parallel to a×b, find m+n.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: The first component makes c=(1/3)(a×b). Hence m=10/3,n=−7/3 and m+n=1.

problems.title: Volume from a diagonal section of a right parallelepiped
problems.question: Base sides are 3,4 at 60°. The smaller diagonal section has area √39. Find volume.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Smaller base diagonal squared=3²+4²−2×3×4cos60°=13; section area=diagonal×height.
steps: Height=√39/√13=√3. The base area is 3×4sin60°=6√3.

problems.title: Recognize a triple-angle identity
problems.question: Solve 3sin x−4sin³x=1.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: sin3x=3sin x−4sin³x.
steps: The equation is sin3x=1, so 3x=π/2+2kπ. Divide by 3.

problems.title: Choose three boys and two girls
problems.question: A camp has 199 students. Which listed product can count five-person groups with three boys and two girls?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: For B boys,G girls, the count is C(B,3)C(G,2), with B+G=199.
steps: A possible split is 100 boys and 99 girls. It gives C(100,3)C(99,2), the listed matching product.

problems.title: A unique solution forced by central symmetry
problems.question: For how many parameters a does x⁴+y⁴=a, cos(x−y)+xy=1 have exactly one real ordered solution?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Both equations are invariant under (x,y)→(−x,−y).
steps: Any nonzero solution has a distinct negative partner, so a unique solution must be (0,0). It forces a=0.
For a=0, the nonnegative fourth powers force x=y=0, and the second equation is satisfied. Thus exactly one parameter works.

problems.title: A regular polygon invariant under a seventy-degree turn
problems.question: What is the smallest vertex count of a regular polygon mapped to itself by rotation 70° about its centre?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The turn must be an integer number of vertex steps: 70n/360=7n/36 is an integer.
steps: Because 7 and 36 are coprime, n must be a positive multiple of 36. The smallest valid polygon has 36 vertices.

problems.title: Spatial coordinates of a bisector foot
problems.question: A=(1,3,2),C=(2,6,5),AB=3,BC=4. BK bisects B and K lies on AC. Find K.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: The weighted coordinate sums are (4+6,12+18,8+15)=(10,30,23). Divide by 7.

problems.title: Intersections with an absolute-input sine
problems.question: Count intersections of f(x)=sin x+sin|x| and g(x)=x²+3πx+2π².
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: For x<0, f(x)=0; for x≥0, f(x)=2sin x.
steps: On the negative half-line, g(x)=(x+π)(x+2π), so intersections occur exactly at −π,−2π.
For x≥0, g(x)≥2π²>2≥f(x), so there are none.

problems.title: Probability that two solution sets are both empty
problems.question: Choose a uniformly from {−7,−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4,5}. Find probability |4x−1|=a²−4 is equivalent to −x²+5x−7≥√(2x−1).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: The quadratic left side of the inequality is −(x−5/2)²−3/4<0.
steps: The inequality is impossible wherever its radical is defined. The absolute-value equation is empty iff a²−4<0, or |a|<2.
The qualifying choices are −1,0,1, three of nine.

problems.title: Count radical-line intersections after a sign check
problems.question: Count intersections of √(x³−5x²−13x+9) and x−3.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Require x≥3; square only after this sign restriction.
steps: Equating squares gives x³−6x²−7x=x(x−7)(x+1)=0.
Only x=7 satisfies x≥3. Direct substitution gives both sides 4.

problems.title: Sum of vectors to three side midpoints
problems.question: A₁,B₁,C₁ are midpoints of BC,AC,AB. For any origin O, OA+OB+OC=p. Find OA₁+OB₁+OC₁.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
formulas: Each midpoint vector is the average of its endpoint vectors.
steps: The sum is [(OB+OC)+(OA+OC)+(OA+OB)]/2=OA+OB+OC=p. O being the incenter is not needed.

problems.title: A possible midpoint of a rotated cube diagonal
problems.question: A cube has side 2, AA₁ on the z axis, AB at 15° to the positive x axis, and B=(a,b,0) with a,b>0. Find a listed possible midpoint of AC₁.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity, then check domains, signs and counting assumptions.
steps: This is one valid orientation. Half the sum of these three edges gives the midpoint (cos15°−sin15°,sin15°+cos15°,1).
The two trigonometric combinations are √2/2 and √6/2 respectively.
